jobs.description: Fully funded 4-year PhD position in experimental and computational philosophy – CONCEPHEX project, University of Seville (Spain)The Department of Philosophy, Logic and Philosophy of Science at the University of Seville invites expressions of interest for a fully funded four-year predoctoral contract within the research project CONCEPHEX, funded by the Spanish State Research Agency (AEI).Please forward this information to anyone you think may be interested.The projectCONCEPHEX (How Concepts Change: Experimental and Computational Approaches in Philosophy of Science and Morality), led by Hugo Viciana and Javier Anta, studies conceptual change by combining conceptual engineering, experimental philosophy, and computational corpus analysis. The project works with leading philosophers and cognitive scientists at institutions such as the Institut Jean Nicod (Paris), the University of Pittsburgh, Macquarie University (Sydney), and the University of Hong Kong. Research stays at some of these partner institutions will be encouraged during the thesis.Possible thesis directionsThe topic of the thesis is open within the broad scope of the project. Possible directions include:Science and morality in historical perspective: studies of historical conceptual change, drawing on historical and contemporary corpora, with applications to the philosophical study of morality and science.The moral psychology of science, including how experts and the general public understand scientific concepts.Experimental studies of how moral concepts vary across populations, with particular emphasis on their interconnections with scientific ideas.The moral psychology of large language models: how they represent and apply moral concepts compared with human populations, and how moral considerations shape their reasoning about scientific evidence.Computational corpus analysis (topic models, transformer-based methods, large language models) to trace the drift of scientific concepts.Methodological questions raised by computational methods in philosophy, such as how to operationalize philosophical orientations and how to assess what models reveal about them.Philosophy learning and computational tools, including generative AI and digital humanities in the teaching of philosophy.Candidates may also propose their own project within this scope. In the statement of interest, please indicate which of these directions you would be willing to work on. Interest in more than one is welcome.What we offerA full employment contract (not a stipend) of up to four years, with full social security coverage, including unemployment benefits. If the thesis is defended within that period, the contract may include a postdoctoral research period of up to 12 months.A gross annual salary of at least 75% of the Spanish public-sector M3 reference category (currently around €25,450).At least €7,000 for research expenses and doctoral tuition fees which may be complemented with additional project funds for research stays.An increasingly international research environment, with Seville's sunshine as an added bonus.Research stays at partner institutions of the project, such as the Institut Jean Nicod (Paris), the University of Pittsburgh, or Macquarie University (Sydney), will be encouraged during their doctoral studies.International Autumn Schools on research methods and several regular research seminars connected to the research topic.Co-supervision by Hugo Viciana and Javier Anta, within the Doctoral Programme in Philosophy of the University of Seville.Teaching. The contract includes collaboration in the department's teaching, typically between 20 and 60 hours per year and up to a maximum of 180 hours over the whole contract, subject to university authorization. Teaching is usually in Spanish, but it can be in English under certain circumstances. Teaching may be waived in the first year when there are good reasons to do so, such as the need to develop sufficient proficiency in Spanish.ProfileA degree and a master's in philosophy, psychology, computer science, or related fields, or equivalent foreign degrees.Candidates must not hold a doctorate and must not have held a predoctoral contract for more than 12 months.Desirable:Interest in contributing to, and helping coordinate, methodological projects on the computational study of concepts in philosophy.English at C1 or C2 level, or equivalent.Expertise in statistical programming, computational corpus analysis, or survey research will be particularly valued.Timeline and how to applyThe formal application will be submitted through the University of Seville's official call, which typically has a very short window of about ten working days.Interested candidates should send a CV and a short statement (max. 600 words) explaining their interest in the position and how their background fits the project, including which of the thesis directions above they would be willing to work on, to[email protected]and[email protected]by 30 November 2026, and preferably sooner. jobs.description: The Department of Psychology at University of Southern Denmark (SDU) is looking for applicants for a PhD fellowship within the field of philosophy, with background in one or more of the following areas: philosophy of psychiatry, philosophy of emotion, phenomenology.We are looking for a person with a relevant degree (M.A., MSc. etc.) in philosophy or a related field. Starting date is September 1st, 2027, or as soon as possible thereafter. The position is fully funded, full-time, for three years. The PhD degree will be awarded by the Faculty of Health Sciences.Research environmentThe PhD student will be based in the research group ofApplied and Interdisciplinary Phenomenologyin the Department of Psychology, SDU, at the Odense campus. The research group develops, disseminates, and applies methods to support cutting-edge research into subjectivity and the nature of human experience. Current group members have backgrounds in philosophy, psychology, anthropology, neuroscience, environmental studies, and pain research.The group directly supports the professional development of its members, most of whom are postdocs or PhD students. In addition to receiving support from the project team, the PhD student will be supported by the broader group to develop their research, presentation, and teaching skills, as well as other academic skills, including those required for organizing academic activities such as workshops and conferences and for successful grant-writing. The PhD student will therefore be provided with the requisite knowledge and skills for pursuing an academic career in Europe or abroad.The PhD student will also be provided with a work computer and a dedicated workspace at the Department of Psychology.Project descriptionThe PhD student will be part of the project, Understanding Experiences of Mood Disturbances in Depression (DEPMOOD), led byAnthony Vincent Fernandez. The project is funded by Independent Research Fund Denmark and runs for four years, starting September 1st, 2026. The PhD student will join the project for the final three years, collaborating with the PI, a psychology postdoc, and several external partners in Europe and the US, including philosophers, clinical psychologists, and psychiatrists.The aim of the project is to establish a taxonomy of the variety of mood disturbances experienced by people diagnosed with depression, providing more precise characterizations of symptoms than those currently offered by concepts such as “depressed mood” or “anhedonia”. The project combines philosophical and qualitative methods, and includes in-depth interviews with people diagnosed with depression. The PhD student will not be expected to carry out interviews, as these will be conducted by the postdoc and external project partners. The PhD student’s primary role will be to help analyze the interview data using a combination of qualitative and philosophical methods. Their PhD thesis will therefore be a theoretical contribution, but will build upon the project’s empirical dataset.In addition to producing a thesis, the PhD student will be required to take a variety of short PhD courses, carry out an international research stay, and fulfil light teaching duties.The PhD student will be provided with DKK 10,000 per year for travel. We strongly recommend that you readHow to apply for a position at SDUbefore you apply.Incomplete applications and applications received after the deadline will neither be considered nor evaluatedClosing date January 15th, 2027 (midnight CET)We expect to conduct interviews within two months of the application closing date.Successful candidates will be asked to send an application to the PhD Secretariat, Faculty of Health Sciences, to be enrolled as PhD students.The PhD programme will be carried out in accordance with Faculty regulations and the Danish Ministerial Order on the PhD Programme at the Universities (PhD order)Salary and Working Conditions at SDUPhD students employed at SDU are employed as PhD fellows according to the Danish Confederation of Professional Associations in public employment (AC) agreement.Salary and any salary supplement are paid according to your seniority level and as negotiated with your union representative. jobs.description: The Research Council of Finland-funded project “the Epistemic Significance of Concepts” based at Theoretical Philosophy at the University of Helsinki invites applications for two (2) fixed-term Postdoctoral Researcher positions. The positions are for four years, starting in April 2027 (or later as agreed).Position descriptionThe positions belong to a research project “the Epistemic Significance of Concepts” led by Academy Professor Maria Lasonen. The project is funded by the Research Council of Finland.The project will work alongside another project on concepts funded by the European Research Council, but its aims are complementary to those of the ERC project.Conceptual resources are crucial from an epistemic perspective. Having the right concepts allows asking the right questions, formulating new hypotheses, and providing good explanations. New concepts are often needed for developing theories that systematize data and make accurate predictions. Good concepts are projectable, providing a sound basis for inductive reasoning. They enable communicating one’s own experiences and recognizing various forms of injustice. In short, concepts enable acquiring knowledge and understanding – whether about the subatomic world, moral reality, or our own social experiences – that is otherwise out of reach. And on the flipside: inapt concepts can result in widespread ignorance. This project aims to ask epistemological questions about concepts in an empirically informed way.These questions include but are not restricted to the following:What are concepts, and what do they allow us to do? What is their epistemic role?How do cognitive scientists and psychologists think about concepts?What are recognitional abilities, and how do they relate to concepts?How are concepts and linguistic meaning related? Can work on lexical competence shed light on conceptual competence?What makes for an epistemically good concept or distinction? Do epistemically good concepts track metaphysically privileged categories?How should considerations of cognitive limitations and architecture inform our account of epistemically good concepts?Could we offer a unified theory of epistemically good concepts that bridges the gap between scientific concepts designating natural kinds and non-scientific concepts with similar epistemic benefits (supporting inductive inference, figuring in good explanations and generalisations, etc.)?Does AI use concepts and if so, how can we tell which concepts it deploys? How can we impact which concepts AI deploys?Can we make rational or reasonable decisions about which new concepts to adopt?What are some robust case studies of new, epistemically good concepts from both the natural and social sciences?How do social practices shape the thinking of individuals by impacting which concepts they deploy and what information is associated with these concepts? How can we understand such social influences in a way that fits with an externalist and referentialist view of language and the mind?What sort of account can we provide of the role of concepts in inference without relying on inferentialism?What can we learn about the distorting view of concepts from the Marxist and feminist traditions and the philosophy of race?How do concepts compete with other concepts?How do concepts relate to unawareness and ignorance?What is the role of concepts in understanding?What is the role of concepts in moral epistemology? Do thick concepts play a special role in moral knowledge and understanding? To what extent does the role of thick concepts in moral epistemology rely on a view about the semantics of thick terms?Since the PI of the project is an epistemologist, the postdoctoral researchers being hired will bring in complementary expertise from outside epistemology.Responsibilities and assessment of qualificationsThe postdoctoral researchers will be responsible forAuthoring peer-reviewed journal articles answering core questions investigated by the project.Being open to collaborating with the other projects members, for instance by writing joint publications.Organizing and participating in international conferences, workshops, and seminars.Preparing competitive grant applications.Providing research-based teaching in Finnish, Swedish, or English(app. 5-10 % of annual working time).Seeking opportunities for societal engagement.Attending a regular project seminar in person.Applications will be assessed according to the following criteria:Applicants should hold a doctoral degreein philosophyor complete a doctoral degree by the beginning of the work contract.Given the salary bracket of the position, the candidates should not have more thanthree years of previous postdoctoral experience.In exceptional cases, we will consider applicants with doctoral degrees in other areas (e.g. cognitive science, psychology, or linguistics), provided they have adequate expertise in philosophy, as well as candidates with more than 3 years of postdoctoral experience.We welcome proposals from researchers with research projects that intersect with a range of the project’s research questions.  A pre-existing interest and publication record on topics within the general theme of the research project is aprerequisite.We are specifically looking for expertise that lies in the intersection of psychology, cognitive science, linguistics (pragmatics, sociolinguistics, psycholinguistics) and philosophy bearing on concepts and word meaning. The aim is to hire at least one researcher with deep knowledge of discussions of concepts and categorization in psychology and cognitive science.Candidates must be able to write and publish high-quality peer-reviewed articles bothindependently and collaboratively.Excellent written and oral communication skills in English are required.Applicants should possess sufficient teaching skills to successfullyteachundergraduate and master programme courses in philosophy.The positions have a six-month trial period.What we offerThe salary for the positions will be based on level 5 of the job requirement scheme for teaching and research personnel in the salary system of Finnish universities. In addition, the appointee will be paid a salary component based on personal performance. The starting salary will be approximately 4000–4400 €/month depending on the appointee’s qualifications and experience.The position will come with a travel budget of 2000 euros per year, to be used for conference travel related to the project.In Finnish universities, the teaching and research staff(app. 65% of total staff) have a special system regarding the free time equivalent to holiday. jobs.description:
The University of North Carolina at Charlotte recognizes the differentiation of mission, goals, and objectives inherent in the diversity of disciplines represented by its colleges and departments. Thus, the Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure Track Faculty should be interpreted in the context of the related departmental and collegiate goals.Teaching, Advising, Curriculum and Instructional Development – Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to teaching may include but are not limited to: subject matter competence, course design, course presentation, advising and consultation, directing student research, curriculum and instructional development, and grading student work.Scholarly Research, Creative, and Other Professional Activities – All tenured and tenure-track faculty are expected to participate in expanding the knowledge base of their academic field by conducting research or engaging in other creative activities as appropriate to the faculty member’s discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to research may include but are not limited to: research/creative activity that generates new knowledge and/or synthesizes and/or integrates existing knowledge, publication, an on-going agenda for research, scholarly, and creative activity, and are expected to seek extramural support for their work.Service to University, the Public, and the Profession – All tenured and tenure-track faculty are expected to engage in a program of service appropriate to their discipline. Faculty responsibilities and essential functions with respect to service may include but are not limited to: service to the administration and governance of the University, public service, and service to the profession.This position is subject to research-security screening. As part of the application, applicants must disclose,either in their CV or in a separate document submitted with the application, all current appointments or affiliations with foreign institutions or organizations, foreign research support, and ongoing research collaborations with foreign institutions, organizations, or their personnel. Before candidates advance to an on-campus interview, the university will review this information and other publicly available information for relationships involving institutions on the current Section 1286 list and any other applicable U.S. restricted-party lists. A disclosed or identified relationship does not automatically disqualify a candidate. As a condition of employment, a selected candidate must resolve any relationship the university determines would violate applicable law or sponsor requirements or materially impair the candidate’s or the university’s eligibility for federal funding.To view the complete Job Responsibilities and Essential Functions for Tenured and Tenure-Track Faculty document visit our website: https://facultyhandbooks.charlotte.edu/full-time-faculty-handbook/


Essential Duties and Responsibilities

The person hired would be expected to be able to teach Ethical Theory at the undergrad and graduate level. The areas of competence are open, but the ability to collaborate with other units on campus is a plus. Standard workload for tenure line faculty is two courses per semester, at all levels from large general education classes to graduate seminars.

jobs.description: Assistant Professor, Philosophy & ReligionJob Type: FacultyJob Number: 00529Location: 1 S Grove St, Westerville, OHDivision: Academic AffairsDESCRIPTIONOtterbein University invites applications for the position of a full-time, tenure track Assistant Professor of Philosophy & Religion. We invite applications from philosophers, scholars of religion, and interdisciplinary teacher-scholars with interests in philosophical ethics, and Buddhism, Hinduism, or other religious traditions of Asia. We seek candidates who will contribute to the department's efforts to enhance diversity and provide an inclusive learning environment for all.RESPONSIBILITIESRESPONSIBILITIES: Teaching load is 3 - 4 which includes teaching courses in Applied and Theoretical Ethics, Religions of India, Buddhism, and other general education courses on topics in Asian philosophical and religious traditions. Candidates should be committed to increasing the diversity of our curriculum and student body. We seek candidates with evidence of success teaching undergraduates, a commitment to recruiting and retaining majors and minors in our department, a commitment to student-centered undergraduate teaching, and the ability to excite students about the study of philosophy and religion. Faculty members are also expected to be involved in professional and community activities for the purposes of scholarship, professional development, student advising and mentorship, and service. New faculty are eligible for a reduced instructional workload during their first year to establish a research program, along with opportunities for ongoing professional development funding and support from our Center for Teaching and Learning.WHEN: This appointment will begin August 2027.QUALIFICATIONSQUALIFICATIONS: Ph.D. in a relevant field of study by the start of appointment. Applicants should have an interest in decolonizing approaches to the study of religion and philosophy and a commitment to social justice-oriented approaches in the classroom. We seek applicants who will complement the existing strengths of our department in analytic philosophy and the Abrahamic religious traditions and who can teach courses in ethics as well as in Asian religious traditions. We are particularly interested in a teacher-scholar who takes a cultural approach to the study of the religions and philosophical traditions of Asia with teaching expertise that emphasizes such areas as the critical study of race, gender, sexuality, and social location.APPLICATION: Submit cover letter, curriculum vitae, three references - including contact information, and a teaching portfolio (including a teaching statement, areas of teaching interest, syllabi and teaching evaluations). As to syllabi, please include syllabi for a course in philosophical ethics as well as a course focusing on an Asian religious tradition, suitable for introductory students. Additionally, a diversity statement is also required, consisting of no more than one single-spaced page, addressing the following two questions: How has a focus on diversity, equity, and inclusion informed your teaching, scholarship, and/or professional experience to date? How do you see yourself contributing to Otterbein's commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion? Priority will be given to applications received by November 20, 2026.ADDITIONAL INFORMATIONDEPARTMENT: The Department is composed of three full-time faculty. One of the full-time faculty is trained in analytic philosophy, the second in religious studies, focusing on Christianity, Islam, and Judaism. The successful applicant for this position will fill the third full-time faculty slot. The Department services one major in Philosophy and Religion and two minors (one in Religion, and one in Philosophy). The bulk of our teaching is to general education students (through the Integrative Studies Program) but we also are connected to the Legal Studies Minor, the Environmental and Sustainability Studies Major, the Honors Program, and the minor in Race and Ethnic Studies.OTTERBEIN UNIVERSITY: Historically progressive. That is the hallmark of Otterbein University and those connected to this private university nestled in the picturesque, historic Uptown Westerville district in central Ohio and minutes away from Columbus, Ohio's largest city. Otterbein has set the pace by providing an educational experience that is progressive, innovative, and inclusive. Students come from towns throughout Ohio, as well as many states and multiple countries, enriching the campus through their individual and collective diversity. As a university that educates students of various racial, ethnic, and cultural backgrounds, we strive for and value a diverse faculty and staff that reflects our student population and Franklin County. Otterbein has been selected as one of 23 universities across the US and the first in Ohio to host a Truth, Racial Healing and Transformation Campus Center. Otterbein will work with its own campus community as well as the Columbus City and Westerville City school districts to create positive narrative change about race; promote racial healing activities; and erase structural barriers to equity and opportunity.Otterbein University is regionally accredited by the Higher Learning Commission (HLC) and is a member of the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools. For more than a decade, Otterbein has been recognized by U.S. News & World Report for its academic quality. In the 2025-2026 U.S. News & World Report Best Colleges rankings, Otterbein ranked #12 among 160 Regional Universities in the Midwest. To learn more about Otterbein, visit http://www.otterbein.edu.WHERE: Otterbein University is located in Westerville, Ohio, a suburb of Columbus, and has received notable national designations, including two appearances on Money Magazine's Top 100 list of Americas' "Best Places to Live" and recognized as one of Forbes "America's Friendliest Towns." Westerville has a population of approximately 38,000 people and combines the beauty and convenience of a medium-sized community with the cultural, educational, and economic benefits of Columbus, the state capital; a thriving and diverse metropolitan area of 2.2 million people. Central Ohio is the fastest growing area in the state with stability provided by a diversified economy.Otterbein University's achievement of academic excellence depends on its commitment to inclusion and belonging. new_jobs.description: Washington University in St. Louis announces the twenty-fifth year of Modeling Interdisciplinary Inquiry, a postdoctoral fellowship program endowed by the Andrew W. Mellon Foundation and designed to encourage interdisciplinary scholarship and teaching across the humanities and interpretive social sciences. We invite applications from recent PhDs, DPhils, or D.F.A.s (with degree in hand by June 30, 2027, and no earlier than June 30, 2024) who have not previously held a research-oriented postdoctoral fellowship. This fellowship program is housed in WashU’s Center for the Humanities. This year we are recruiting two fellows. We are interested in interdisciplinary scholars whose research has a focus on global issues including but not limited to global public humanities methods.In mid-August 2027 the newly selected Fellows will join the interdisciplinary community at the Center for the Humanities. Each fellowship is anticipated to run for two academic years. Postdoctoral Fellows pursue their own continuing research in association with a senior faculty mentor at WU. During the two years of their fellowship, they will teach two courses. Fellows are expected to remain in residence during all semesters of their appointment.Applicants should submit, through Interfolio, a cover letter, a curriculum vitae, and a description of their research program (no more than 1000 words and accessible to reviewers in other disciplines). Applicants who have not completed their doctoral work should indicate, in their cover letter, how many chapters of their dissertation are complete and how complete the remaining chapters are. Please include the names and email addresses of three references.Application: https://apply.interfolio.com/195936

new_jobs.description: About UsGeorgia College & State University (GCSU) is the state's designated public liberal arts university, where students learn the essential skills to compete in a fast-paced and technology-driven global society.
